title: Data-Free Metrics Don't Work: The Missing Invariance Under Functionally Preserving Reparameterisations
abstract: arXiv:2611.15621v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Data-free methods for analysing and understanding the layers of neural networks offer many metrics for quantifying notions of 'strong' versus 'weak' layers, with the promise of increased interpretability. In particular, random matrix theory (RMT) offers data-free metrics that claim predictive power over the quality of pre-trained models at a layerwise precision and the ability to identify model pathologies, indicating a unique relationship with generalisation. As a result, metrics from RMT are championed for pre-training optimisation strategies and post-training compression. We establish that RMT-based metrics are unrelated to performance or training by showing that functionally preserving reparametrisations of a pre-trained model can have arbitrary metrics. We show this across a range of architectures and scales. To create functionally preserving reparametrisations, we exploit the well-established phenomenon of criticality: some layer

translated_title: 无数据指标不起作用：功能保持重参数化下缺失的不变性
translated_abstract: 用于分析和理解神经网络各层的无数据方法提供了许多指标来量化“强”层与“弱”层的概念，并有望提高可解释性。特别是，随机矩阵理论（RMT）提供了无数据指标，声称能够以逐层精度预测预训练模型的质量，并能够识别模型病理，表明其与泛化能力之间存在独特的关系。因此，来自RMT的指标被推崇用于预训练优化策略和训练后压缩。我们通过证明预训练模型的功能保持重参数化可以具有任意的指标值，确立了基于RMT的指标与性能或训练无关。我们在一系列架构和规模上展示了这一点。为了创建功能保持重参数化，我们利用了已被充分研究的临界性现象：某些层……
tldr: 本文证明基于随机矩阵理论的无数据指标与模型性能和训练无关，因为对预训练模型进行功能保持的重参数化可以任意改变这些指标的值。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes that RMT-based data-free metrics are unrelated to model performance or training, since functionally preserving reparameterisations of a pre-trained model can have arbitrary metric values.
